properties.description: Dater's Handbook (2016) is a television romantic comedy-drama directed by James Head and starring Meghan Markle, Kristoffer Polaha, and Jonathan Scarfe. The film follows a successful businesswoman who, urged on by her sister, uses a dating handbook and dates multiple men to test its rules, leading her to reassess her priorities and what she truly wants in a partner. The movie blends lighthearted humor and heartfelt character moments while gently satirizing the self-help dating industry. Its tone is warm and optimistic, grounded in playful chemistry and relational discovery.
properties.plot_summary: A successful businesswoman, encouraged by her sister, turns to a popular dating handbook to fix her rocky love life and deliberately dates several men to test its rules. As she cycles through different suitors she confronts her own priorities and the gaps between practical checklists and real attraction. The experiment forces her to re-evaluate what she truly wants in a partner and how honest she can be with herself and others. Along the way warm moments and playful chemistry complicate the neat categories the book promises.

properties.description: Branagh Theatre Live: Romeo and Juliet (2016), directed by Kenneth Branagh, presents a staged, black-and-white broadcast of Shakespeare's tragic romance starring Richard Madden, Lily James, and Derek Jacobi. The production transposes the tale into a period-inflected aesthetic with stylized staging and cinematic touches while retaining the core story of two young lovers caught between feuding families. Themes of forbidden love, fate, and impulsive youth are emphasized through heightened performance choices and a melancholic visual palette. The result is an emotionally intense theatrical adaptation that foregrounds passion and loss.
properties.plot_summary: Two teenagers from rival houses fall in love and attempt to pursue a private relationship despite a long-standing family feud. Miscommunication, impulsive choices, and a sense of inexorable fate amplify the violence around them. The tale ends in tragedy, underscoring the human cost of entrenched hostility and youthful passion.

properties.description: Lady Chatterley's Lover (2015), directed by Jed Mercurio and starring Holliday Grainger, Richard Madden and James Norton, is a period romantic drama adapted from D.H. Lawrence's novel. Set in the years after the First World War, it follows a married woman whose husband's war injury and impotence leave her emotionally and sexually estranged, leading her into a passionate affair with the estate's gamekeeper. The film foregrounds class conflict, sexual longing and personal autonomy, using understated performances and atmospheric cinematography to create a bittersweet, emotionally charged tone.
properties.plot_summary: Constance marries a wealthy colliery owner who returns from the Great War disabled and largely withdrawn from their marriage. Excluded from the running of the estate and denied intimacy by her husband's impotence, she grows increasingly alienated and vulnerable. A plain-spoken former miner employed as the estate's gamekeeper awakens in her the passion and companionship she lacks, and their clandestine affair leads to betrayal and an unexpected pregnancy. Forced to choose between a comfortable but joyless life and an uncertain future with the man she loves, she must confront class expectations and the consequences of desire.

properties.description: Look Both Ways (2022), directed by Wanuri Kahiu and starring Lili Reinhart, Danny Ramirez, and Aisha Dee, is a tonal blend of romantic drama and speculative fantasy that follows a college graduate whose life diverges into two parallel timelines. One timeline follows an unexpected pregnancy and life in her hometown; the other follows a move to Los Angeles to pursue a dream career. Through alternating scenes the film examines choices about love, career, and parenthood, offering a reflective, hopeful perspective on identity and acceptance. The result is an intimate, character-driven story that balances humor and poignancy.
properties.plot_summary: On the eve of her college graduation, a young woman’s life splits into two parallel realities: in one she becomes pregnant and stays in her hometown to raise her child, and in the other she moves to Los Angeles to pursue her dream career. Each timeline explores different relationships, setbacks, and moments of growth as she confronts the consequences of that single divergence. The film alternates between the two lives to examine how choices shape identity, responsibility, and self-acceptance, ultimately delivering a quietly hopeful message about resilience and agency.

properties.description: Ben Is Back (2018), directed by Peter Hedges and starring Julia Roberts and Lucas Hedges, is a drama about a young man who leaves rehab for 24 hours to spend Christmas Eve with his family. The film follows the tense reunion and the frantic unraveling of secrets that test familial bonds, highlighting powerful performances and a realistic, low-key visual approach. It explores themes of addiction, relapse, motherhood, guilt and the social dimensions of the opioid crisis, delivering an emotionally charged portrait of a family under pressure. The emotional tone shifts between tender warmth and anxious urgency, driven by intimate, performance-led scenes.
properties.plot_summary: A troubled young man leaves rehab for 24 hours to spend Christmas Eve with his family, but his return reopens old wounds and unsettles everyone at home. His mother, desperate and fiercely protective, tries to keep him safe while confronting painful truths about his past and the sources of his addiction. What begins as a tense domestic reunion gradually unspools into a low-key, suspenseful search through the city for people and choices that threaten his sobriety. The film examines the cost of addiction on family, the cycle of relapse, and the fraught hope of recovery.
